profile.what: The former WABCO India: India's leading maker of air-brake and air-management systems for trucks, buses, trailers, tractors and off-highway machines (compressors, valves, brake actuators and chambers, ABS, EBS, ESC, ECAS air suspension, AMT clutch actuation, door controls), plus a spares business, exports of goods (mostly to the parent) and engineering/software services exported to ZF group centres. Promoter: WABCO Asia Pvt Ltd, Singapore (60.00%), a ZF Friedrichshafen AG company (ZF bought WABCO Holdings in 2020).
profile.lines: FY26 revenue Rs4,119 cr: domestic OEM Rs1,978 cr (48%), aftermarket Rs584 cr (14%), exports of goods Rs1,025 cr (25%), services Rs504 cr (12%: software Rs324 cr, R&D Rs60 cr, business support Rs77 cr, other Rs44 cr), other operating revenue Rs28 cr.
profile.footprint: Six plants (Ambattur, Mahindra World City SEZ and Oragadam in Chennai; Jamshedpur, Lucknow, Pantnagar), a proving ground near Chennai, 3 engineering and technology centres with 1,100+ engineers, ~550 aftermarket dealers/distributors and ~270 authorised service partners; 5,560+ people (1,999 permanent employees on the company's rolls at Mar-2026). Wholly owned subsidiary ZF CV Control Systems Manufacturing India Pvt Ltd (Oragadam; FY26 revenue Rs83.9 cr, PAT Rs10.5 cr).
profile.share: ZF group in India claims ~80% share in CV braking solutions (meet p11) and ~50% in pneumatic braking for construction equipment (meet p20); ABS is fitted on all its OEM trucks.

callPoints: Revenue from operations +9.3% (total income +5.7%): domestic OEM +8.6% against CV>6T production +8.4%, despite a 9% fall in trailer demand and a shortage of blue-collar labour in April-May; aftermarket Rs158.4 cr (+15.6%) with a record month in June (Rs63.1 cr); exports of goods Rs271.4 cr (+9.7%) as US and European truck markets fell ~10%; services +12.5%.
PAT Rs104.5 cr (-14.7%) because Q1FY26 held a Rs39 cr FX gain on services billing plus Rs4.7 cr of one-offs (Rs43.7 cr in all); excluding FX and one-offs, PBT rose 16.9% to Rs140.8 cr.

Costs: aluminium rose from ~Rs260/kg to >Rs360/kg (easing ~Rs25 in July); gas, oil, grease, rubber and plastics up. Part recovered from OEMs (already in Q1), the rest 'under active discussion' (normally a two-quarter lag, longer this time); selective aftermarket price increases from July-2026; PERFORM26 cost programme.

ESC: nominated by three major OEMs for pneumatic ESC (12V and 24V systems) ahead of the truck mandate; ZF expects to keep its 'majority position'; localisation 40-50% now, >75% by start of production (Q3 of next year). ADAS/AEBS can be bought separately from braking, so ZF's share there is not assured.
Demand: July CV production ~40,000-42,000 vehicles, ~10,000 above a typical July; August-September 'at par levels'.
People: CFO Sweta Agarwal left; Rakesh Mishra appointed CFO from 1-Sep-2026; C.V. Kavviya whole-time company secretary from 25-Jul-2026.

guidance.said: CFO: 'I would expect it to be more or less flattish with maybe single-digit small growth for the next year... I would be cautious on the call out for financial year '26-'27' (Middle East war, commodity costs).
Rs180-190 cr in FY27: new products, replacements and upgrades.
ESC already mandatory on buses (except Type 1 city buses) since Sep-2025; all vehicles >6 tonnes from Oct-2027; ZF has full-suite ADAS awards from two OEMs.
Americas -22% and Europe +6% in Q4FY26; sales split ~50:50 US/Europe; expect 'an increase in the trend' but a ~20% gap to the volumes of two years ago.
Growth 'should remain at this level' (~7.5% q/q, +12.5% y/y) on vehicle solutions, brake controls, cybersecurity work from India.
One portion of commodity/FX inflation recovered; the rest 'something that we will be securing over the next quarter'.

history.what: Began as the brakes division of Sundaram-Clayton (TVS group) with WABCO technology; became WABCO-TVS, then WABCO India, a separately listed company (incorporated 2004) under WABCO's majority control
history.impact: Six decades as the incumbent air-brake supplier to Indian truck and bus makers; WABCO Asia Pvt Ltd, Singapore, held 75% until 2024

history.what: ZF Friedrichshafen buys WABCO Holdings worldwide (2020); WABCO India joins ZF's Commercial Vehicle Solutions division and is renamed ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems India (2022)
history.impact: The parent's global commercial-vehicle business now sources goods and engineering services from the Indian company

history.what: BS-VI transition and Covid: CV production collapsed
history.impact: Revenue -32% in FY20 and -3% in FY21; EPS fell from Rs24.8 (FY19) to Rs9.1 (FY21, post-bonus basis)

history.what: New capacity at Oragadam and Mahindra World City (SEZ, exports) and an ESC test track at the ZF Proving Ground near Chennai
history.impact: Capex Rs130-200 cr a year; depreciation up from Rs90 cr (FY21) to Rs132 cr (FY26)

history.what: Promoter sell-downs: 75.00% to 67.49% (Jun-2024), 63.16% (Dec-2024) and 60.00% (6-Jun-2025, 600,133 shares in the open market)
history.impact: Free float up from 25% to 40%; Indian mutual funds now own ~24%

history.what: Shareholders approve related-party transactions with ZF CV Systems Global GmbH of up to Rs2,500 cr in FY27 (postal ballot, 20-Mar-2026)
history.impact: FY26 transactions with that one group company: Rs1,351 cr (33% of revenue)
Shares x6 to 11.38 crore; all per-share figures in this report are post-bonus
